# Build a Bot

# **What Can a Bot Do?**

Here's what you can enable a SeaTalk bot to do:

* Send and receive messages in**1-on-1 chats**.
* Be**added to group chats by its users**and be removed by any group member.
* **Send messages to group chats**.
* Be**mentioned**by other group members in group chats and receive those messages.

Let's take a look at how to quickly build a bot capability.

# **Step 1: Create a Bot**

From [open.seatalk.io](https://open.seatalk.io/), click on "Start building" or "Create app" to trigger the app creation wizard. You can also trigger this by clicking "Create app" from you app list. Follow the steps in the wizard to complete the basic configuration of your app.

Step 1: Basic app information

![](data:image/png;base64,)

Step 2: Service and data scope configuration

![](data:image/png;base64,)

Your new app will have a default status of Not Configured. [Learn more about app statuses.](https://open.test.seatalk.io/docs/SOP-App-Statuses) Click the Enable button in the Bot card in the Capability section.

![](data:image/png;base64,)

![](data:image/png;base64,)

Once a capability is successfully enabled, it will appear in the menu on the left hand side of the page, and you will be directed to the capability configuration menu of the newly added capability. Additionally, default API permissions for the capability will be enabled for your app.

# **Step 2: Configure Event Callback**

You will need to set up an**Event Callback** system to receive notifications of important events, such as receiving messages in 1-1 chats and group chats. You can refer to [this article](https://open.seatalk.io/docs/server-apis-event-callback)for a more detailed explanation of how it works.

**Step 2.1:**Go to**Advanced Settings -> Event Callback** and click the**Edit** icon next to the URL text box to configure the callback URL for the bot.

****

**Step 2.2:**Supported events will be automatically enabled for the bot after a callback URL is successfully configured.

****

# **Step 3: Interact with Your Bot's Users in 1-on-1 Chats**

* **Receive messages:**When a user sends a message to your bot in 1-on-1 chat, you will receive a "[Message Received From Bot User](https://open.seatalk.io/docs/event_message_received_from_bot_subscriber)" event callback from SeaTalk.
* **Send messages:**You can send a text message to your bot's user through the "[Send Message To Bot User](https://open.seatalk.io/docs/messaging_send-message-to-bot-subscriber)" API using HTTP requests.

# **Step 4: Interact with Users in Group Chats**

**Bot users**can add a bot into group chats to facilitate interactions and automate tasks. Below listed what a SeaTalk group chat bot can do:

* Being notified when:

  * A bot user has**added the bot to a group** via "[Bot Added to Group Chat](https://open.seatalk.io/docs/event-bot-added-to-group-chat)" event callback.
  * A group member has**@mentioned the bot** in a group via "[New Mentioned Message Received From Group Chat](https://open.seatalk.io/docs/event_new_mentioned_message_from_group_chat)" event callback.
  * The bot has been**removed from a group** via "[Bot Removed From Group Chat](https://open.seatalk.io/docs/Event-Bot-Removed-From-Group-Chat)" event callback.
* **Send messages** to a group chat via "[Send Message to Group Chat](https://open.seatalk.io/docs/Send-Message-to-Group-Chat)" API.
* **Obtain basic information about the group chat**, such as the group name, group settings and member list via "[Get Group Info](https://open.seatalk.io/docs/get-group-info)" API.
* **Obtain the group chat histories** via "[Get Chat History](https://open.seatalk.io/docs/get-chat-history)" API. (***Remarks*** *:* *Please note that this API permission is restricted to apps that have* ***obtained approval from management*** *due to the sensitivity nature of chat history.*)

## **How to a** **dd a bot to a group**

* Bots can be added into a group chat by its users just like adding a contact.
* When your bot is added to a group chat, you will receive a "[Bot Added to Group Chat](https://open.seatalk.io/docs/event-bot-added-to-group-chat)" event callback from SeaTalk.

****

<u>Desktop/Web</u>



## **How to remove** **a bot from a group**

* Bots can be removed from a group chat by any group members just like removing a user.
* When your bot is removed from a group chat, you will receive a "[Bot Removed From Group Chat](https://open.seatalk.io/docs/Event-Bot-Removed-From-Group-Chat)" event callback from SeaTalk.

# FAQ - Compatibility with lower SeaTalk Client Version

When users interact with bots in a group chat using the SeaTalk Client App version lower than 3.33, they may experience slight differences in how it appears on their client platforms. Here's a summary of how it looks:

<u>iOS:</u>

* Lacking the display of “Bot” indicator in following places:

  * Main Chatroom View
  * Group Member List
  * Pin Message List
  * Combined Forwarded Chat History
  * For Later List
  * Search Results
  * Message Info Page
* Bots will appear in the "Select Member" list but may prompt an "User cannot be reached" error toast when selected.

<u>Android:</u>

1. Lacking the display of “Bot” indicator in following places:

   * Group Member List
   * Pin Message List
   * Combined Forwarded Chat History
   * For Later List
   * In-chat Search Results
   * Message Info Page
   * @Mention List
2. Bots can be chosen to transfer group ownership to but may return error without a toast message.
3. Bots are displayed in the message info page.

<u>Desktop/Web:</u>

1. Lacking the display of “Bot” indicator in following places:

   * Pin Message List
   * Combined Forwarded Chat History
   * For Later List
   * @Mention List
2. Bots can be chosen to be set as a group admin but may prompt an "Unable to change role" error toast.
3. Bots can be chosen to transfer group ownership to but may return error without a toast message
4. Bots can be chosen to be added as a contact from the group member list but may prompt a "Request to be contact failed" error toast.
